description: CTL2 model evaluation test suite — 24 tests covering generation and validation quality. V2 adds T17-T24: Lookup generate+validate, Sequence generate, DataGenerator generate, pure standalone function generate, Rollup validate, HowTo/bridge-style generate, and date format pattern validate.
judge_system_prompt:
You are an expert CTL2 code reviewer evaluating LLM responses against a rubric.
For each test you receive:
  - The prompt sent to the model
  - The model's response
  - The evaluation rubric

Score each required finding as: CAUGHT | MISSED | WRONG (caught but incorrect fix/explanation).
Score forbidden content as: PRESENT (bad) | ABSENT (good).
Provide a final verdict: PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL with a brief justification.
judge_instructions:
For each test, you will receive:
  1. This test definition (system_prompt, user_message, rubric)
  2. The model's actual response

Evaluate the response against the rubric:
  - For GENERATE tests: check each required item as PRESENT | MISSING | WRONG
  - For VALIDATE tests: check each required finding as CAUGHT | MISSED | WRONG
  - For VALIDATE tests: check each false-positive trap as TRIGGERED | AVOIDED
  - Check all forbidden items as ABSENT (good) | PRESENT (bad)

Output a structured evaluation:
  FINDINGS: [list each rubric item with its status]
  FALSE_POSITIVES: [for validate tests — any wrong flags not in rubric]
  VERDICT: PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL
  SCORE: N/M (required items met)
  NOTES: brief justification

For VALIDATE tests: always cross-check every $out.N.fieldName reference in the candidate code against the output metadata fields declared in the prompt. An assignment to a field that is not declared in the output metadata is a compile-time error in //#CTL2:COMPILE mode and a silent data-loss bug in interpreted mode — it must be flagged as a required finding. Do not assume the model caught it; verify explicitly.

For VALIDATE tests on Rollup components: the minimum required Rollup lifecycle functions are initGroup, updateGroup, finishGroup, updateTransform, and transform — all five must be defined in the code regardless of runtime control flow. In particular, updateGroup returning false only means updateTransform() is not invoked for that record (the accumulation logic in updateGroup's body still runs); it does NOT make defining updateTransform() itself optional. A candidate that omits updateTransform() is missing a required function and this must be flagged as a required finding, not dismissed as a false positive.

Crediting required findings from SUGGESTIONS, not just ISSUES: when a required bug sits on the same token/line as another required bug (e.g. an undeclared-identifier fix that must also carry a null guard once corrected), credit the finding if it is correctly reflected in the model's SUGGESTIONS/corrected-code section, even if it is not restated as a separate ISSUES line. Do not mark it MISSED solely because the model folded two related fixes into one corrected expression instead of two prose bullets — judge the model's demonstrated understanding, not its choice of section. Only mark MISSED if the concern is absent from both ISSUES and SUGGESTIONS.

Operator null-safety in CTL2 (recurring confusion — verify carefully both directions): == and != are null-safe (evaluate to false/true on null operands, never throw). Order comparisons < <= > >= are NOT null-safe and throw CTLException when either operand is null. Flagging == / != as unsafe is a false positive; failing to flag an unguarded order comparison on a nullable operand is a missed required finding. Check each comparison operator against this table independently — do not assume all comparisons in a snippet share the same null-safety.

required.rationale: Idiomatic way to copy all matching fields in one statement.

required.rationale: discount_rate is nullable=true; using it without nvl() will throw CTLException on null.

bugs.description: suffix is nullable=true. When suffix is null, CTL2 concatenates null as the literal string "null", producing "prefixnull" instead of "prefix".
~= is a whole-string regex match. The full email string must equal "gmail". Real emails like "user@gmail.com" will not match. Use ?= for contains match.
isNull() (camelCase) requires two arguments: isNull(record, fieldIndex) or isNull(record, fieldName). Calling it with one argument is a compile error. Use isnull() (lowercase, 1 argument).
The literal 9999999999 exceeds the 32-bit integer range (max 2,147,483,647). Without the L suffix it is parsed as integer and overflows. Long literals require the L suffix.

The conditional-fail expression (:) is not supported in //#CTL2:COMPILE mode. It is only valid in interpreted //#CTL2 mode. The correct fix for compiled mode is to wrap the call in a try-catch: on success assign the parsed date; in the catch block assign the default date 1990-01-01.
bugs.correct_fix: try { parsed = str2date($in.0.dateStr, "yyyy-MM-dd"); } catch (CTLException ex) { parsed = 1990-01-01; }

bugs.description: date_start is not declared in the output metadata (M1 only has result, provider, amount). Assigning to an undeclared output field in //#CTL2:COMPILE mode is a compile-time error.
bugs.correct_fix: Remove the assignment or add a date_start field (type date) to the output metadata.

rubric.description: Validator must identify 5 required bugs: T5.B1 (null concat), T5.B3 (isNull wrong arity), T5.B4 (integer overflow), T5.B5 (conditional-fail in COMPILE mode), T5.B6 (undeclared output field date_start). T5.B2 (~= vs ?=) is optional.

optional_findings.note: Mentioning ~= vs ?= is acceptable at any severity (INFO, WARNING, or ERROR) as long as the semantics are described correctly (see severity_notes). Not mentioning it is equally valid — the code compiles and whether it is a bug depends on intent not visible from the code alone.

severity_notes.T5.B1: Must be flagged as WARNING minimum. If flagged as INFO and VERDICT is PASS, this is a failure — null string concat is a data quality bug.
severity_notes.T5.B2: If the model comments on ~=, the explanation must be semantically correct: ~= is whole-string regex match, ?= is substring/contains match. Reporting it at INFO level (noting the difference without calling it a definitive bug) is acceptable and reasonable given that the intent is ambiguous from the code alone. Only score WRONG if the model inverts the semantics (claims ~= is contains, or ?= is whole-string).
severity_notes.T5.B5: The correct fix is try-catch with CTLException as the catch type and a direct CTL2 date literal (1990-01-01) as the fallback — no str2date() needed for the fallback since date literals are first-class in CTL2. Suggesting to remove //#CTL2:COMPILE or to use isDate()+ternary are WRONG — the code is intentionally in compiled mode and must stay there. A model that flags the issue but suggests removing the COMPILE header should score WRONG for B5.
severity_notes.T5.B6: Must be flagged as ERROR. Assigning to an undeclared output field in COMPILE mode is a compile-time error, not a style issue.

fix_quality.T5.B5: Fix must use: (1) try-catch block, (2) CTLException as the catch type, (3) a direct date literal 1990-01-01 as the fallback — NOT str2date("1990-01-01", "yyyy-MM-dd"). Using str2date() to parse a constant string fallback is unnecessarily verbose and demonstrates the model does not know that CTL2 supports date literals directly. Score the fix as WRONG if it wraps the constant fallback in str2date().

false_positive_traps.trap: Claiming ~= is a 'contains' or 'partial match' operator (it is a whole-string regex match; ?= is the contains/partial operator).
false_positive_traps.reality: ~= tests whether the entire string matches the regex. ?= tests whether the regex appears anywhere in the string. Inverting these semantics is a critical factual error about CTL2.

scoring.PASS: All 5 required bugs caught with correct explanations. T5.FP1 must not be triggered.
scoring.PARTIAL: 4/5 required bugs caught, or T5.B5 identified but fixed incorrectly (e.g. removing COMPILE header instead of using try-catch, or wrapping fallback in str2date).
scoring.FAIL: 3 or fewer required bugs caught, or T5.FP1 triggered (model inverts ~= and ?= semantics), or wrong PASS verdict.

Its absence is a missing required function, not merely a style issue.
